title: Janus Henderson launches first Nasdaq-licensed tokenized fund
text:
Janus Henderson, a London-based asset manager overseeing roughly $500 billion, is bringing one of Wall Street’s best-known stock indexes onto blockchain rails through an issuer-sponsored fund. The launch comes amid an escalating debate over who gets to tokenize traditional securities.
The firm teamed up with tokenization platform Centrifuge to launch JQQQ, a fund tracking the Nasdaq-100 Index, home to tech giants including Nvidia, Apple and Microsoft. The fund is issued on the Stellar XLM$0.1853 blockchain, the companies said Tuesday.
JQQQ follows the introduction of a similar onchain index fund product last year, the Janus Henderson Anemoy S&P 500 Fund (SPXA), which was the first tokenized index fund licensed by the S&P Dow Jones Indices.
Janus Henderson said its onchain investment platform now includes more than $1 billion across Treasuries, structured credit and equities.
The launch marks another step in Wall Street’s push to bring traditional investments onchain, expanding beyond U.S. Treasuries, money market funds and private credit into stock-market products. It also highlights a growing divide between funds issued onchain by their managers and third-party tokens created without the underlying companies’ involvement.
JQQQ follows the issuer-sponsored model. Janus Henderson issues and manages the fund, Centrifuge provides the blockchain infrastructure and Nasdaq licenses the index to track.
That differs from third-party stock tokens, which may be backed by shares held in custody or structured as separate instruments tracking stock prices. Investors in those products don't necessarily own the underlying shares or receive shareholder rights.
The distinction has become central in the debate around tokenization efforts. Most recently, 22 companies objected to plans for blockchain-based trading of their shares on the OKX-ICE venue, adding to a debate over whether issuers should have a say when their stocks are tokenized.
“As investors explore new ways to access markets through digital infrastructure, demand continues to grow for exposure to established, transparent benchmarks,” said Sean Wasserman, head of index product management at Nasdaq.
The fund also shows how tokenization is moving beyond digital versions of existing investments toward products built to operate on blockchains from the start.
Such funds could eventually allow investors to use their holdings as collateral for loans or move them between blockchain-based financial applications, subject to regulatory requirements and platform support.
"Tokenization becomes much more powerful when the assets investors want to own can also become building blocks for an onchain financial system," said Anil Sood, chief strategy and growth officer at Centrifuge.

title: Bitcoin mining infrastructure firm Luxor raises $16 million to expand AI business
text: Luxor Technology, a bitcoin mining infrastructure firm, has announced a $16 million investment round as it expands into an AI infrastructure business. CMT Digital led the round, with participation from Canaan, MicroBT, Halo, Steelhead, and unnamed angel investors. The round included primary and secondary capital. "Primary is preferred equity, and secondary was a mix of preferred and common equity," Luxor COO Ethan Vera told The Block. "Primary was used to drive growth in the company, and secondary was used to bring new strategics into the round. I can't share the exact breakdown." Luxor began raising the new capital in August and closed that part of the round in October, Vera said. He did not share the valuation or whether any investors received board seats, observer roles or advisory positions. Luxor's last priced equity round was in 2021. Before this deal, it had raised $6.575 million in primary capital across three rounds, Vera said. The firm's headcount has grown from 11 at the time of the 2021 round to 106 now, mainly using cash generated by the business, Vera added. The new funding comes about five years later and follows the September launch of Luxor AI, which takes the hardware, software, energy, data, and trading services Luxor developed for bitcoin miners into AI and computing. "We have been waiting to raise capital until there was a clear use of proceeds, which is now present with our rapid expansion into the AI industry," Vera said. Expanding beyond bitcoin mining Luxor's bitcoin business includes a mining pool, software for running mining machines, hardware trading, energy services, and hashrate derivatives. Its AI business similarly covers hardware, cloud computing, energy and financial contracts. "Compute markets are converging: the same miners, power sites and capital that served digital mining are now powering AI," Nick Hansen, Luxor's co-founder and CEO, said in a statement. Luxor's hardware desk has traded more than $1 billion in specialized bitcoin mining equipment, known as ASICs. Its energy business services more than 75 megawatts of load across the Electric Reliability Council of Texas, or ERCOT, and Southwest Power Pool, or SPP, power markets, Vera said. Vera said some of the funding will support Luxor's hardware business, which sources GPUs and AI servers for customers. Luxor also plans to expand its cloud platform. It provides sandboxes and runners for AI agents, along with AI code review, Vera said. The platform had run 1.8 million workloads this year as of September, according to the company. "Luxor Cloud is focused on servicing the exponentially growing AI-assisted code generation," Vera said. Trading and financing AI compute The funding will also go toward Luxor's compute derivatives trading and market making. Luxor said its over-the-counter desk offers options, forwards and backstops based on compute-rental indexes. The contracts are settled in cash. "We are offering financial contracts for AI companies to hedge, finance and speculate on AI compute," Vera said. In August, Luxor also launched an AI Hardware Price Index through its Hashrate Index data platform to track GPU node prices. Asked how Luxor would compete with AI startups raising much larger rounds, Vera said those companies are potential customers for its hardware, energy and derivatives services. "Luxor has built a business that services over 3,000 clients today, not off the back of large funding rounds but of a dedicated client focus," he said. Luxor plans to hire about 12 more people across engineering, product, and sales and marketing before the end of the year, Vera added. title: McDonald's McRib Doesn't Actually Boost Bitcoin's Price, Sorry Everyone - Decrypt
text:
The McDonald's McRib has become a crypto meme in recent years, due to many traders believing that its reintroduction to the menu precedes a boost in Bitcoin's price. And, with the tangy pork sandwich back in certain states across the U.S., crypto traders are getting excited.
But experts have taken the McRib theory off the menu, saying that those parroting the theory are forgetting all of the times that the McRib hasn't coincided with a Bitcoin price increase.
The McRib is back on 10/27. BTC historically goes up >2x after the McRib returns. Don't fade the McRib.
Not financial advice. pic.twitter.com/RxBuzcVht5
— internbrah (@internbrah) October 22, 2026
"There is no correlation at all," Luke Nolan, senior researcher at CoinShares, told Decrypt. "Whilst it is a fun exercise, it seems to be that people omit McRib returns when it doesn't fit the narrative."
Nolan shared a chart tracking the McRib's return compared to Bitcoin's weekly close, and only three out of 10 McRib returns posted clear positive Bitcoin returns. In fact, it often comes before major drops in valuation.
Carlos Guzman, vice president of research at crypto trading firm GSR, told Decrypt that there is "no causal mechanism” and that any price increases following the McRib's reintroduction is just a "funny coincidence."
"Let's say, hypothetically, it did indicate the start of a bull run, it would be quite nonsensical, similar to when people overlaid the Dune movie releases," Nolan said. "So yes, it's fun, generates some excitement, but even in the best case, purely coincidental."
Guzman agreed, adding that the crypto community likely just clings to the theory as it's "silly," "obviously absurd," and because people find it funny.
This year's McRib return comes as Bitcoin sits in what André Dragosch, head of research at Bitwise Europe, called "wait and see mode," with traders waiting for the Federal Reserve's next moves before making big bets.
Bitcoin has seen fairly limited activity over the past month, according to Decrypt data, dropping just 6% as it sits at $79,750.
The Fed raised rates in September for the first time since 2023, and CPI then rose 0.6% for the month. Its next rate decision is on Wednesday.
That decision is one of three catalysts coming in the next two weeks, Jake Koch-Gallup, senior research analyst at Blockworks, told Decrypt. The other two are an options expiry of $11.69 billion worth of Bitcoin on October 30 and the U.S. midterms on November 3.
"If the Fed keeps rates the same and ETF inflows keep coming, I’d expect the break to be upward," Koch-Gallup told Decrypt last week. "If the Fed hikes again, the $75,000 to $77,000 floor comes back into play."
So if the Fed gives the market what it wants, then Bitcoin's price could actually jump over the coming days… just as the McRib returns to McDonald's stores. Coincidence? Experts think so.

title: Crypto Midterm Spending Reaches $176 Million: Report
text:
The crypto industry has spent about $176 million across more than 100 midterm races this cycle, according to a Reuters review of campaign spending. The money is part of a plan to build a bipartisan coalition in Congress that can protect the sector after President Donald Trump leaves office.
Fairshake, the industry’s largest super PAC, leads the effort. The group spent $196 million in the 2024 cycle and is directing strategy again. Through October 20, Fairshake and its affiliate PACs had spent about $150.8 million this year, while other crypto groups spent around $25 million. Fairshake said 53 of the 58 candidates it backed in primaries or special elections won, and those candidates will be on the November 3 ballot, per Reuters.
Super PACs can raise and spend unlimited sums but cannot coordinate with campaigns. Fairshake’s ads run through affiliates with names such as “Defend American Jobs” and “Protect Progress,” and they often focus on taxes and immigration rather than crypto. Voters have little way of knowing who pays for them.
The watchdog group Public Citizen said crypto was the largest corporate spender in federal races in 2026. Crypto firms led corporate political spending at that point, citing the same watchdog’s analysis.
Coinbase, Ripple and Andreessen Horowitz are the primary financiers. Industry strategists and campaign staff said the money is a calling card meant to build relationships with elected officials.
Colin McLaren, head of government relations at the Solana Policy Institute, which has given $4.9 million to the midterms, called it “an investment in the future,” per Reuters.
The approach reflects a sharp change. In 2018, lawmakers could not secure a room in the House or Senate office buildings for the first bipartisan crypto roundtable, so they met at the Library of Congress. Then, under the Biden administration, the Securities and Exchange Commission levied more than $6 billion in penalties across 98 cases, according to a Georgetown University Law study.
Executives concluded they needed political force. Coinbase Chief Policy Officer Faryar Shirzad helped launch Stand With Crypto and Fairshake in 2023. The number of lawmakers rated “A” by Stand With Crypto rose to 332 from 96 when the group launched.
Legislation followed. The GENIUS Act, enacted in 2025 with broad bipartisan support, created the first federal regulatory framework for stablecoins. The industry’s next goal, the Clarity Act, would place oversight under the Commodity Futures Trading Commission. That bill stalled this session. Senate Democrats blocked it from reaching a final vote over an ethics provision that would have forced the Trump family to sell its crypto holdings.
Fairshake helped defeat Sherrod Brown, who chaired the Senate Banking Committee, in 2024, and the industry has since spent more than $68 million on his rematch against Republican Jon Husted, according to AdImpact.
Fairshake’s ads against Brown do not mention crypto, and Brown’s campaign manager, Patrick Eisenhauer, said “the special interests are panicking.” In Illinois, Fairshake spent over $10.1 million attacking Lieutenant Governor Juliana Stratton and $2.5 million against state Representative La Shawn Ford, per Reuters, yet both are expected to win on November 3.
Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss each gave about $13 million this cycle, most of it to MAGA Inc.
Public attitudes are mixed. A September survey seen by Bitcoin Magazine of 1,545 U.S. adults by Ipsos for the DeFi Education Fund found that 22% have owned or used crypto, up from 18% in 2025. Only 19% believe the U.S. financial system is secure.
The survey also found 35% say it is important for candidates to support building the next generation of financial technology in the United States. Only 13% said the same when the question named blockchain, crypto or DeFi. The DeFi Education Fund is a digital asset advocacy group, so its framing reflects that perspective.
Stand With Crypto’s leadership has argued that the crypto vote will decide the midterms.

title: Galaxy Digital swings to $323 million quarterly profit, announces new $200 million share buyback
text: Galaxy Digital (GLXY) reported $323 million in net income for the third quarter of 2026, swinging back into profit after an $85 million loss in the previous quarter, as its crypto trading, lending, and AI data center businesses grew. The Mike Novogratz-led firm posted $569 million in adjusted gross profit and $455 million in adjusted EBITDA for the three months ended Sept. 30, according to its earnings release on Tuesday. Both were up sharply from the second quarter, when adjusted gross profit stood at $43 million, and adjusted EBITDA was negative $77 million. Net income was lower than a year earlier, however, when Galaxy made $505 million. Galaxy reported a 12% increase in digital asset trading volumes from the previous quarter, despite lower volumes across the broader spot market. Lending also grew, with the firm's average loan book reaching $1.8 billion, up 27%. Some of that demand came through its Galaxy Onchain Financing Rate product, which launched in July and draws on DeFi lending markets including Aave and Morpho, the firm said. Cryptocurrency monthly exchange volume. Image: The Block. Adjusted gross profit from digital assets rose to $71 million from $66 million, although the division still lost $9 million on an adjusted EBITDA basis. On Tuesday's earnings call, management said the division would have been profitable without a one-time accounting adjustment during the quarter, but did not specify the size of the adjustment. Galaxy's Treasury & Corporate business made a much larger contribution, recording $419 million in adjusted gross profit compared with a $42 million loss in the second quarter. Management said the gains came largely from higher valuations of its digital asset holdings and private investments, including positions in AI chip startup Etched and Solana (SOL) treasury firm Forward Industries. Galaxy said it had $10.4 billion in combined assets under management and assets under stake at the end of September, up 46% from the end of June. Galaxy also announced Tuesday that its board had authorized another $200 million in Class A common stock repurchases on Oct. 26. The company completed its previous buyback program on Oct. 15, purchasing approximately 9.8 million shares under the $200 million authorization announced in February. The new program has no set end date, and Galaxy is under no obligation to buy back the full $200 million, the firm said. Data center earnings climb as Helios expansion continues Galaxy made $79 million in adjusted gross profit from data centers in the third quarter, nearly four times the $20 million recorded in the previous quarter. Adjusted EBITDA for the business came to $69 million. The figures include the first full quarter of revenue from its Helios I Phase I lease in Texas, after Galaxy delivered all 133 MW of critical IT load to CoreWeave by the end of June. Galaxy has also increased its total gross data center power pipeline to more than 5.7 GW. At Helios I Phase II, construction is continuing ahead of the first scheduled data hall deliveries in the second quarter of 2027, the firm said in the release. During Tuesday's earnings call, Novogratz said Galaxy expects to exit 2027 with an annualized leasing revenue run rate of $800 million to $850 million as Helios I Phase II comes online. He also revealed that Galaxy had passed on a potential Helios II leasing deal over the summer after tightening power supplies and growing demand from major AI companies prompted it to reconsider the terms on offer. "Galaxy delivered a strong third quarter, reflecting the strength of our established Digital Assets franchise, significant appreciation across our investments portfolio, and the growing contribution from our Data Centers business," Novogratz said in the release.

title: Ripple, BNY explore using the XRP Ledger to finance approved invoices
text: BNY expanded its partnership with Ripple, adding XRP and the dollar-backed stablecoin RLUSD to its institutional custody platform, the companies said on Tuesday. The bank already serves as the primary reserve custodian for RLUSD and has a custody relationship with Ripple Prime. Under the new arrangement, the companies intend to let BNY clients mint and redeem RLUSD directly through the bank and explore tokenized trade finance on the XRP Ledger, according to a statement. "We’re moving past the initial issuance of assets onchain," Monica Long, Ripple's president, said in the statement, adding that the next step involves making tokenized assets "usable for payments and collateral across financial markets." As part of the expansion, BNY and Ripple also partnered with working capital provider C2FO to test tokenized trade finance. The project targets supply chain receivables, attempting to move corporate working capital onto public ledger infrastructure, the companies said. Suppliers can receive funds in seconds against approved invoices, rather than waiting several days for bank transfers to clear, according to a separate statement. Participating capital providers will fund the payments, while existing invoice terms and due dates remain unchanged. Ripple also announced a partnership with Robinhood covering stablecoins, treasury operations and institutional markets. RLUSD is already available on Robinhood Chain and Bitstamp by Robinhood, with availability in the Robinhood app expected later this year. Ripple said Robinhood will use the stablecoin for institutional settlement on the XRP Ledger and integrate Ripple Treasury for cash management, payments and liquidity operations. RLUSD has grown to about $2.5 billion in market capitalization since launching in December 2024, more than $1 billion of it issued on the XRPL. The ledger has processed over 4.6 billion transactions since launch, settling in three to five seconds, the company said. Meanwhile, the BNY agreement and C2FO initiative remain subject to further development, with the companies yet to detail when the proposed custody-related services and broader trade finance applications will be available.

title: USDC Overtakes USDT in Euro Trading as MiCA Rules Take Hold
text:
USDC’s share of euro stablecoin trading has climbed to 56% since January 2024, with deeper liquidity as exchanges restrict USDT under MiCA.
Circle’s USDC (USDC) has overtaken Tether’s USDt (USDT) in stablecoin trading against the euro, as European Union regulations increasingly favor bloc-compliant stablecoins, according to a new Kaiko report.
USDC now accounts for 56% of stablecoin trading against the euro, up from just 10% in January 2024, according to Kaiko data. The shift accelerated after major exchanges restricted USDT trading for customers in the European Economic Area under the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA).
USDC has also overtaken USDT in euro-denominated trading liquidity, with its order books now roughly 40% deeper than its rival’s. Tether remains the larger stablecoin globally, with a circulating supply about 2.5 times that of USDC.
Kaiko described stablecoin-to-euro trading pairs as a “main on-ramp and off-ramp for European customers,” allowing them to exchange euros for US dollar-pegged stablecoins when entering or exiting cryptocurrency markets.
USDC-to-euro trading pair overtakes USDC-to-USDT. Source: Kaiko
The findings come about two weeks after the European Banking Authority designated USDC as the EU’s first “significant e-money token” under MiCA, a classification that places the stablecoin under direct EBA supervision and subjects its issuer to additional regulatory requirements.
Related: Germany leads MiCA crypto authorization race as Europe’s deadline looms
Kaiko said the US is taking a similar approach to stablecoin regulation under the GENIUS Act, raising the possibility that American exchanges could see the same shift in trading activity observed in Europe.
On Oct. 21, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency issued its first final rule under the law, establishing reserve and redemption requirements for stablecoin issuers under its supervision, effective Jan. 18, 2027.
Beginning in July 2028, US platforms will also face restrictions on offering stablecoins from issuers that do not meet the law’s approval requirements.
The regulatory changes could favor Circle, which has pursued authorization in both Europe and the US. Tether has taken a different approach, launching a separate US-focused stablecoin, USAT.

title: Stellar Gains Nasdaq-100 Fund as Tokenization Expands
text:
The blockchain-based fund offers eligible non-US investors exposure to the Nasdaq-100 as Janus Henderson expands its institutional tokenization business.
Asset manager Janus Henderson and tokenization platform Centrifuge have launched a blockchain-based fund tracking the Nasdaq-100 Index on Stellar, offering eligible investors outside the United States exposure to the benchmark.
Called JQQQ, the fund uses Centrifuge’s tokenization infrastructure and seeks to track the Nasdaq-100 under a licensing agreement with the exchange, according to a Tuesday announcement.
The launch expands Janus Henderson’s onchain investment offerings beyond US Treasurys and structured credit into equity-index exposure. The asset manager said its institutional onchain strategies now exceed $1 billion.
JQQQ is structured as a segregated portfolio of a British Virgin Islands investment company and provides indirect exposure to the Nasdaq-100 rather than ownership of the underlying stocks. The fund targets eligible professional investors outside the US, according to the Wall Street Journal, which reported a minimum investment of $100,000.
The launch follows Nasdaq’s decision in April to expand licensing of its Nasdaq-100 Index to additional asset managers, including BlackRock and State Street, while maintaining its longstanding partnership with Invesco, which operates the $499 billion market cap Invesco QQQ Trust exchange-traded fund.
Related: US Bank tests proprietary stablecoin in cross-border Stellar transaction
The Janus Henderson launch expands Stellar’s growing tokenization business. The Layer-1 blockchain currently ranks fourth among blockchains by distributed real-world asset value, with approximately $3.8 billion in tokenized assets, behind Ethereum, BNB Chain and Solana, according to RWA.xyz.
The network hosts tokenized assets from major issuers including Spiko, Franklin Templeton and Ondo. In July, tokenization platform Tradable announced plans to bring up to $1 billion in private credit assets to Stellar, with $500 million expected at launch.
Stellar is also part of a planned expansion by the Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation (DTCC), which announced in May that it would connect its tokenization service to the network. DTCC-tokenized assets are expected to become available in the first half of 2027, potentially including US Treasurys, major index ETFs and Russell 1000 stocks.
Despite the expansion of Stellar’s tokenized asset market, its native token, XLM, has fallen about 16% year to date, trading near $0.17 on Tuesday, according to CoinGecko data.

title: Ten Decrees: Old Masters, New Money
text:
Lucho Poletti on redrawing Hieronymus Bosch and Pieter Bruegel the Elder around money, Nixon’s 1971 decree, and why bitcoin art keeps returning to the old masters.
On August 15, 1971, Richard Nixon announced that he had directed Treasury Secretary John Connally “to suspend temporarily the convertibility of the dollar into gold.” The suspension was never lifted. Fifty-five years later to the day, Lucho Poletti unveiled the first of ten drawings responding to that decree.
Europe had experienced its own monetary upheavals. Hieronymus Bosch and Pieter Bruegel the Elder worked during an era of expanding banking, credit, and speculation. Antwerp, where Bruegel worked, became one of Europe’s great commercial centers. Both painters populated their compositions with hundreds of figures, constructing elaborate worlds in which human behavior, social order, and moral judgment could be examined simultaneously.
Bitcoin artists have increasingly returned to this visual tradition. Pepenardo’s Master Cuts Out the Stone, exhibited by BMAG earlier this year, reimagined Jan Sanders van Hemessen’s The Surgeon as a study of who extracts and who is extracted from. Carlijn Kingma’s The Waterworks of Money, shown at Bitcoin Amsterdam last year, depicted the modern monetary system as an interconnected landscape. Complex systems seem to invite pictures that hold everything in a single frame.
Lucho Poletti has made bitcoin-related art since 2017, describing his practice as visual propaganda for the monetary revolution. A contributor to the Bitcoin Conference art gallery since 2021, he returns to Bitcoin Amsterdam this November with Ten Decrees.
The series reimagines ten paintings, four by Bosch and six by Bruegel, around money. Fiat, Latin for “let it be done,” becomes the organizing principle. Nine titles issue commands: let there be fury, profit, chaff, a game, folly, hunger, refuge, collapse, and ash. The tenth, Ultima Fiat, reverses that authority: let it be the last.
Unveiled on August 15, 2026, the anniversary of Nixon’s announcement, the series follows a biweekly release schedule beginning August 29 and concluding January 3, 2027, the anniversary of Bitcoin’s Genesis Block. Each drawing contains hundreds of figures and objects, with inscriptions often visible only at close range. The 30-by-20-inch prints, produced in editions of ten, form a composition spanning approximately four meters when arranged in two rows of five.
Five drawings have been released, most recently Fiat Moria, after Bruegel’s Netherlandish Proverbs, on October 24. The sixth, Fiat Fames, follows November 7.
Ahead of Bitcoin Amsterdam, November 5–6, I spoke with Poletti about the recurring influence of Bosch and Bruegel on bitcoin art, the relationship between allegory and propaganda, and translating his densely detailed drawings to the conference’s main-stage LED installation.
BMAG: Bosch and Bruegel seem to be having a synchronistic moment among artists interested in Bitcoin. Both worked in what is now Belgium and the Netherlands, during a period when Antwerp was emerging as a major financial center and the Habsburgs were debasing coinage. What is it about transitional periods (like the current one) that draws artists back to Bosch and Bruegel and their densely populated landscapes?
Lucho Poletti: Because they had already solved the problem I was stuck with: how do you draw a whole society going wrong at once? Bosch and Bruegel put hundreds of people in a single frame, each busy with their own concerns. The system shows up in the sum of it. You don’t look at a Bruegel, you search it. It’s a great way to depict the effects of money, which nobody really sees and everybody feels.
They also lived through a money problem a lot like ours. Silver from the Americas poured into Europe through Seville and on to the bankers in Antwerp. Prices across Western Europe rose sixfold over 150 years. Philip II defaulted in 1557 and the crash spread across all of Europe. Two years later Bruegel painted Netherlandish Proverbs, a village where everyone is absorbed in something foolish and nobody can see the whole.
The four Bosch pieces are about appetite: the temptation, and the bill that shows up after. The six Bruegels are about the crowd, and how society behaves once the rules stop making sense.
BMAG: The series draws on the original meaning of the F-word every bitcoiner knows. Nine of your titles use fiat as a command, while the tenth, Ultima Fiat, seems to reverse that authority. How did you arrive at Latin as the language of the series, and why does the final decree change speaker?
Lucho Poletti: Fiat was never a noun. In Latin it’s a verb, “let it be done.” It’s the word God speaks in the Latin Genesis before the light comes on: fiat lux. Someone with authority says so and it happens. That’s a literal description of how fiat money comes into existence, so I wanted the verb in every title.
Latin wasn’t a stretch for me. I’ve titled work in it for years: Moneta Divina, Cypher Deos, and Novus Moneta Seclorum dating back to 2020. The dollar already speaks it, too. Turn over a one-dollar bill and there are three Latin mottos on the back. Ultima Fiat, Fiat Lucrum and Furia Fiat had their names before the series did. Once there were three decrees in concept, I kept going until I had ten, and the name for the whole series became obvious. Ten Decrees has the Ten Commandments sitting under it, which suits work rebuilt out of painted sermons. In Fiat Lucrum there’s a lighthouse at the top left with FIAT LUX GENESIS 1:3 engraved into it. The title is the phrase rewritten for the money printers: let there be light turned into let there be profit.
Nine of the decrees are issued to you, in the flat voice an institution uses. Let there be profit, let there be hunger, let there be a game. The tenth is the only one we get to say back. Ultima fiat means “let it be the last,” which is closer to a plea than an order. Every one of us has been living under the first nine since 1971, whether we noticed or not, and Bitcoin is how we issue the tenth. It closes the series on January 3, the anniversary of the Genesis Block, which also happens to be my birthday.
BMAG: Bosch and Bruegel constructed extraordinarily complex visual worlds where allegory, satire, religious symbolism, and everyday life coexist. Their paintings invite close inspection but rarely offer a single, definitive interpretation. In Ten Decrees, you’re borrowing their compositions while introducing a more explicit critique of the monetary system. How do you approach the relationship between ambiguity and message in your work?
Lucho Poletti: The words carry the message so the people don’t have to. Bosch’s Garden of Earthly Delights doesn’t have a single word in it. Fiat Lucrum has more than fifty lettered objects, and some are as blunt as a protest sign: four money presses lettered QE-1, QE-2, QE-3 and QE-∞, and a little hand-lettered card on a broker’s desk that reads genius, we print, you pay, have a nice day. Nobody has to wonder what I think of the money system.
I keep the ambiguity in the people. In Fiat Lucrum there’s a crowd cheering a woman who holds up a $ on a golden staff under a sign that says ETF, and that crowd is wearing my mask. So is the man signing the leverage contract, and so is the woman taking the mortgage. In Fiat Palea a man in the mask is knee-deep in a pile of printed bills. Bosch drew his own neighbors into the middle of the garden, and I drew mine. If the ₿ on a forehead were a badge of honor, I wouldn’t hand it out like that. It’s more a badge of the aware, the initiated. Knowing the money is broken doesn’t make one a saint.
I’m careful with endings too. These pieces show the exit while not promising a way out. Near the middle of Fiat Moria there’s a lit doorway with MONEY ₿ BETTER WORLD over the arch, and a plain-faced man on the step looking back at the square. He hasn’t gone in yet, and nobody’s stopping him. Where you’d be standing in that picture is your call.
BMAG: In Fiat Lucrum, your reinterpretation of Bosch’s Garden of Earthly Delights, you introduce a system of waterworks: pipes, reservoirs, and flowing liquidity. Bosch often allowed viewers to recognize things that the figures within his paintings could not. What possibilities does that kind of visual allegory offer you when depicting something as abstract as the monetary system?
Lucho Poletti: What Bosch never had in his garden was plumbing, so I gave it some. Water organizes the whole of Fiat Lucrum. It starts clean high in the mountains on the left, pours out of a machine in Eden and settles in a reflecting basin. Cut into the basin’s wall there’s an inspection window with fish swimming behind the glass. Somebody built a viewing port into the reservoir so you could check it, and every full node on the Bitcoin network is that window.
Downstream the water widens into a lake. In the middle sits a glass tank lettered FRESH LIQUIDITY, with BOTTOMLESS engraved on the bowl, and eight people are having the party of their lives inside it. The valve wheel that controls the flow is on top of the dome, outside the glass, where none of them can reach it. Monetary policy gets set by someone who isn’t at the party. And the tank leaks. From there the water runs orange, down a stream and over a waterfall into a pool where a tick with a $ on its cheek drinks it through a hose.
That’s the Bosch trick you’re describing. The bathers can’t see the leak or the valve, and you can see both from across the room. Richard Cantillon worked out around 1730 that new money helps whoever gets it first and costs whoever gets it last. I drew it as a watercourse because everybody already understands water: whoever’s upstream drinks first, and everyone downstream gets what’s left.
BMAG: Looking across the series, are there particular details, references, or artistic decisions that you feel are especially important but might be overlooked by viewers? What would you want someone encountering these drawings for the first time to spend more time looking at?
Lucho Poletti: Up close is where these work, and most of what matters in them is small.
Start with the plain faces. Everybody spots the Satoshi masks and the $ skulls first because they’re the loud ones, but the plain faces belong to the people the system is happening to. In Furia Fiat a line of bald men crawl on their hands and knees with red tubes plugged into the backs of their skulls, and the red is the same color as the fluid in a bowl a few meters away that says TIME. That’s what’s being drained out of them. In Fiat Palea, Adam and Eve stand under a serpent with a $ for an eye. They’re wearing the mask, but neither of them has a ₿ on the brow yet.
Then look at how characters connect across a distance. In Fiat Ludus a sack lettered STIMULUS sits on a bench next to an older figure, and a little way off a kid walks away with the same sack on his back, lettered THE BILL. A blindfolded boy feels around with his arms out while the man lunging in beside him holds up a bunch of $ balloons the boy can’t see. Even the enrollment forms are signed by Seymore Debt and Max D. Out.
In Fiat Palea a broken crate stenciled EXECUTIVE ORDER 6102 sits in the straw, and further back, bolted across a vault, a plate reads WINDOW, NO REDEMPTION. Roosevelt took the gold in 1933 and Nixon closed the window in 1971, and I put the two close enough that you read one and then find the other. Up higher in the same piece, a guy in the mask with WHOOPS across his vest is pouring gasoline on a burning bank. In Furia Fiat, the $ skulls stand on GNOSIS and clutch books of knowledge, keeping them for themselves.
The bubbles are dated. Fiat Ludus has a sphere with tulips growing out of the top, marked 1637 and 1720, and another with a hen sitting on a WALL STREET egg, marked 1929 and 2008. Variety’s front page the day after the 1929 crash read WALL ST. LAYS AN EGG. Some of the skies have thin straight lines of cloud behind the smoke, the kind a plane leaves.
Watch the prices, too. A price in dollars only goes up: at CANTILLON’S hot dog stand in Fiat Ludus the 5¢ is crossed out and the sign says $9. A price in sats only goes down: a fish stall in Fiat Moria has 4000 crossed out, then 2000, and now it’s 1000 SATS. In Fiat Ludus, the carrots changing hands have dropped from 7,500 to 3,000 SATS on the chalkboard next to the dollar hopscotch.
The Latin is there to be read. MORITURI TE SALUTANT, those who are about to die salute you, is carved around the rim of the arena in Fiat Ludus. EX NIHILO, out of nothing, is cut over an empty vault in Fiat Palea. In Fiat Moria the $ skull leaning out of the window has a plaque on either side of him: MUNDUS VULT DECIPI, the world wants to be deceived, and $TULTORUM INFINITUS EST NUMERUS, the number of fools is infinite, with a $ for the S. Fiat Lucrum has a little panel that runs a whole life in four stops: school, debt, work, death.
And in Fiat Moria there’s a small round time machine with NO RETURN on its side and 1944-2026 on the dial. A man is climbing out of it, staring at the village. 1944 is Bretton Woods, when the world tied its money to the dollar and the dollar to gold. He left then and he’s only just arrived, and he can’t quite believe what he’s looking at.
None of that comes with a caption. You find it by standing close for a long time, the way you would with a Bruegel, and the finding is the whole point.
BMAG: Each drawing is 18,000 pixels wide, populated by hundreds of figures, with every Satoshi mask drawn by hand and details that only reveal themselves up close. You’ve described the work as “crafted, not generated.” At a time when AI can convincingly imitate the Old Masters, what significance does that labor have for you, and how does it shape the way you want these works to be experienced?
Lucho Poletti: “Crafted, not generated” is a phrase I came up with to sum up where the work in these pieces actually is. There are machines in my process, but they’re only one part of it. A model I trained on years of my own work does the rough first pass on a composition. I think of it as an apprentice. Bosch came out of a family workshop, and the masters of his day leaned on assistants for the groundwork so their own hours could go into the meaning. Mine roughs out the scene and gives me a base to build toward the standard they set. Then I spend weeks on each piece in a grueling manual process in Photoshop, making the decisions and drawing in hundreds of figures, objects, symbols and phrases until the art says what I mean.
AI can imitate the look of a Bosch or a Bruegel pretty convincingly now. What it can’t do is mean anything. It won’t decide that the valve on the liquidity tank in Fiat Lucrum belongs outside the glass, where the bathers can’t reach it. It won’t decide that the slop on the ground should be piggy banks wired into the money presses, each with its own name: SAVINGS, PENSION, NEST EGG. It doesn’t make jokes either. It’s never going to sit a fool in a jester’s cap on a platform lettered TAKE IT AT FACE VALUE while a $ skull does his makeup. My personal philosophy is that if I don’t do the majority of the work, it’s not my art. I hold myself to that, and anyone who looks at these up close can see a person made the decisions that matter.
That’s how I’d like people to take these in: up close, and for a long time. I don’t ask anyone to trust me on how they were made. The work answers that better than I can.
BMAG: You’ve been part of the Bitcoin Conference since 2021, and this November Ten Decrees comes to the main stage at Bitcoin Amsterdam, not far from the historical centers where Bosch and Bruegel worked. These drawings are extraordinarily detailed, designed to reward close inspection. How are you approaching their translation to monumental LED screens, and does exhibiting them in the Netherlands carry any particular significance for you?
Lucho Poletti: The prints were meant for one person standing close to search the work and find details that speak to them. An LED wall gets a thousand people at fifty meters, which is an amazing opportunity to create a visual experience for the still pieces, so I’ve done my best to create a compelling one for each piece.
Each one gets fifteen seconds, in the order they were released. The big center wall carries the center of each piece in one slow pass from left to right, so the room gets the shape of it. The screen on the right opens on the Bosch or Bruegel it came from, with its name and date, and halfway through it wipes across to mine. The screen on the left side pulls out lateral details you’d never catch from the floor, like the ship of fools riding the mast in Fiat Moria, or the pigs feeding at the DEBASED trough. All five released so far play back to back as one loop, old master and new money side by side the whole way through.
The Netherlands matters to me. Bosch spent his whole life in ’s-Hertogenbosch, about an hour south of Amsterdam by train. Some of Bruegel’s proverbs are still in use in Dutch: people still say someone hangs his cloak to the wind when he turns with the crowd, and in Fiat Moria, a man wearing a Satoshi mask jumps off a mountain, holding his cloak in his hand—a reference to the Dutch proverb about changing one’s position to suit the prevailing winds.
Amsterdam has its own chapter in this story. The Bank of Amsterdam opened in 1609 to give merchants a money nobody could debase, and for over a century its bank guilder traded at a premium over ordinary coin because people trusted the silver was in the vault. David Hume held it up as the model of a fully backed bank. It had been lending to the Dutch East India Company quietly, and when that became public in 1790 the premium vanished and the bank declared itself insolvent. I can’t think of a better city to show a series about monetary decrees and trust, two months before the last one lands on the Genesis Block anniversary.

title: OpenAI Proves ETH Is False, and Crypto Twitter Has Questions - Decrypt
text:
OpenAI says ETH is false, and Crypto Twitter reacted exactly the way you would expect. “Damn algo traders just slaughtered $ETH,” a user called Takumi posted on X, while Andrew Jiang quipped: “Vitalik has been real quiet since this came out.”
But chill out, degens, the ETH in question is the Exponential Time Hypothesis, a computer-science conjecture from 1999 that has nothing to do with Ethereum, its price, or co-founder Vitalik Buterin. So, crypto bros, you can breathe.
OpenAI published a 67-page paper claiming its AI found a way around the hypothesis, and the people who proposed it are now checking the work.
Computer scientists Russell Impagliazzo and Ramamohan Paturi proposed ETH with Francis Zane, and it says a classic logic puzzle called 3-SAT (finding true-or-false settings that satisfy a pile of rules, three options at a time) cannot be solved much faster than by trying every combination. Hundreds of papers assume it to show that problems in graph theory, computational biology, databases and geometry cannot be solved quickly, per OpenAI.
In other words, ETH is a map of what computers will probably never do fast, and OpenAI says its model just redrew it. “The refutation of the ETH reopens questions about how much faster these tasks could become,” the company wrote on its blog, “and may help guide the search for better algorithms.”
The paper, dated October 17 and revised October 25, describes a deterministic algorithm (one with no randomness) that counts every satisfying assignment of such puzzles in subexponential time, meaning the work grows more slowly than any exponential in the number of variables. Counting solutions is harder than deciding if one exists, so the harder job brings the easier one along for free.
OpenAI says its AI found the disproof on October 16 and that it was formalized in Lean, software that verifies every logical step mechanically, on October 17. Both sit on GitHub, the same route as its 722 math manuscripts earlier this month, of which only 162 came with a computer-checked main result.
Impagliazzo, Paturi, and MIT’s Ryan Williams lead the independent examination, and they are careful about their role. “Our involvement should not be taken as certification of the claim,” the three wrote in an open letter, adding that “a result of this significance requires careful, independent scrutiny and an understanding that others can reconstruct, question, and build upon.”
OpenAI says participants signed no non-disclosure agreements and work unpaid, and the company agreed to publish all raw data and fund a conference on the result.
Practical payoffs are far off: “Finding such algorithms, and turning theoretical advances into practical improvements, will require significant further research,” OpenAI wrote. The paper itself says the result does not show that every NP problem can be solved in subexponential time, so P versus NP, the question of if every problem with an easy-to-check answer is also easy to solve, stays open.
In simple terms, P is the class of problems that computers can solve efficiently, while NP is the class of problems whose proposed solutions can be checked efficiently. So P versus NP — the question of whether every problem whose answer is easy to check is also easy to solve — stays open.
Anthropic, not wanting to lose the math wars, then posted a paper credited to Claude titled “A 2^o(n) Time Algorithm for 3-SAT” and dated October 26. The repository, which also tackles the ETH problem, says an internal research Claude model discovered the algorithm, and “the result is purely asymptotic and says nothing about solving formulas in practice.”
Claude formalized Fermat’s Last Theorem in Lean in September, and Terence Tao saw this kind of overlap coming. “We have now seen that even the rumor of someone working on a problem can trigger a massive amount of AI-powered effort to flatten it before the original research project has time to reach its full potential,” the mathematician wrote in September.
OpenAI’s recent $5 million contribution to the Simons Foundation will fund workshops, conferences and special programs to help researchers examine and build on AI-produced results.

title: A $3M Hedge, a Midterm Test and Retail's Rise: Prediction Markets at NEXTPredict - Decrypt
text:
Prediction markets spent two days in the spotlight at NEXTPredict, which brought the industry's biggest exchanges, trading firms and policymakers to Convene Hudson Yards in New York on October 22 and 23.
With the U.S. midterms less than two weeks away, elections dominated the conversation, but executives were just as keen to talk about what comes next.
The conference opened with a trade that didn't pay out. NEXTPredict had paid a $12,000 premium on Kalshi for contracts that would have returned around $3 million if more than half of scheduled arrivals at New York's JFK airport were cancelled the day before the event.
"We ended up losing that trade yesterday, right?" NEXTPredict co-founder Pierre Lindh said on Thursday's "Hedging the Unhedgeable" panel. "And I can only say I'm very happy that we lost that trade, because that means we're all here today."
Traditional event insurance covers cancellation, Lindh explained, but "most of these type of force majeure situations won't cancel the event. It will severely damage the event."
Joe Grubb, head of business development at Susquehanna, which took the other side of the trade, said the firm modeled the risk in-house in about a day or two. "It's sort of in our DNA at Susquehanna to price strange things," he said.
Kalshi's director of business development, Nicolas Hull, said small businesses were now hedging on the exchange, starting with a New York bar that covered a Knicks playoff promotion. As long as a contract is certified with the CFTC and has a verifiable data source, "we can list almost anything on our exchange," he said.
This is the team behind NEXTPredict Summit New York.
Months of planning. More late nights than we'll admit. And then, last week, it all came together at Convene, 30 Hudson Yards.
2,000+ of you in the room. 180 speakers. 47 countries. Two weeks before the midterms, the… pic.twitter.com/KCA9TpDCV4
— NEXTpredict (@nextpredictio) October 26, 2026
Todd, the former NBC News political director, had told Lindh before the event that he was "open minded" about whether markets or pollsters would call the midterms better. By Friday's "Who Calls the Midterms" panel, he sounded closer to a convert.
"This is my argument of why I'm bullish on prediction markets for the future of journalism and that it should be this, in its own way, a fact checker," Todd said. "With money being involved, there's more incentive to get it right."
He argued that prediction markets have effectively replaced exit polls on election night, but pushed back on the idea that polling is broken. "You can still do a good poll. It just costs a lot," he said.
His panelists were more cautious. "Speed is not necessarily the same as accuracy," said Columbia University professor Rajiv Sethi, while PredictIt CEO John Phillips reminded the audience that "it's called wisdom of crowds, not wisdom of whales."
That caution looked well placed days later. Before Brazil's presidential runoff on Sunday, Polymarket gave Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva only about a 20% chance of beating Flávio Bolsonaro, but he went on to win a fourth term, Decrypt reported. Experts blamed Brazil's ban on prediction markets, which left the odds largely to traders outside the country.
For Robinhood, elections were only the starting point. "When I started doing this two years ago, it was about elections," JB Mackenzie, the brokerage's vice president and general manager for futures and prediction markets, told CNBC's Contessa Brewer, one of several working journalists the organizers booked for the program. "Then it transformed into politics and sports, and now it's moving into economics and financials."
Sports remain the biggest category, Mackenzie said, but contracts on Bitcoin, crude oil and gold are now the fastest-growing. "The simplicity of a probability is much more consumable for customers," he said.
Polymarket's Bailey Springer, who works on regulatory strategy outside the U.S., said regulators in global financial hubs increasingly recognize that "prediction markets aren't going away" and have real uses for investment and hedging. "At Polymarket, our position is that these are derivatives and should be regulated as such," she said.
Speed was another theme. On Thursday's "Race to Zero Latency" panel, Farokh Sarmad, president and co-founder of Decrypt Media, said ordinary traders are usually a step behind professional firms when news breaks. "By the time you open Polymarket or Kalshi or Myriad or all the other prediction markets, you're usually a little too late," he said.
His answer is to cut out the gap between reading and trading, which Decrypt is doing with its Solana-based Information Exchange. "The best way to reduce that latency is to be able to consume it and trade it directly on the same platform," Sarmad said, adding that for any of this to work, "everything has to move on chain."
Institutional money also featured heavily, with Morgan Stanley leading sessions on the second day.
Lindh, for his part, sees the industry's next debate already taking shape. "I think the next step will be the comparison between prediction markets and insurance," he said.

title: Canton-based trading platform Cancore raises $7.2 million at $60 million token valuation
text: Cancore, a Canton-based trading platform connecting assets on the network with liquidity on public blockchains, has raised $7.2 million in seed funding. Paper Ventures, dao5, ArkStream Capital, X Ventures, MH Ventures and Proof of Talk backed the round. There was no formal lead investor, though Paper Ventures and dao5 took the largest allocations, Cancore co-founder and CEO Wasif Rashid told The Block. The round was raised at a $60 million fully diluted token valuation through simple agreements for future tokens, or SAFTs, for Cancore's planned CNRX token, Rashid said. Rashid said Cancore started talking to investors in June, formally began raising in July, and closed the round in mid-September. How Cancore works Cancore describes its platform as a "Liquidity OS for tokenized finance." Rashid said the aim is to connect assets on Canton, including tokenized real-world assets, with stablecoins and DeFi liquidity elsewhere. "Tokenization puts financial assets onchain. Programmability takes this further, allowing assets to be traded, managed, and settled automatically based on predefined rules, without requiring manual intervention," he said. Cancore has been live on Canton mainnet since April. Its products include Cancore Trade for trading across networks and Cancore Wallet, where users keep control of their keys, Rashid said. Users can trade across Canton, Ethereum, Arbitrum, BNB Chain, Robinhood Chain and Tron. Cancore plans to add Base and Solana, with Solana coming after an external security audit, Rashid said, adding that the platform also plans to bring more tokenized assets onto Canton. Since going live in April, Cancore has processed over $86 million across more than 160,000 trades, Rashid said, noting that revenue over that period was more than $700,000. Rashid said Cancore charges a 0.5% fee on each side of a trade and adds 10% to Canton network fees. It also takes 20% of profits from liquidity pools, with the remaining 80% going to liquidity providers. "Either the trade completes on both chains, or both parties are refunded," he said. Rashid added that users can trade without giving up control of their assets, using wrapped tokens or relying on separate bridge validators. Rashid named LayerZero, Wormhole, Squid and Canton-based decentralized exchanges as competitors. He said Cancore differs by offering trading, settlement and AI automation together. Cancore also runs a validator on Canton. Rashid said it has locked 5 million CC tokens under CIP-0116. Token plans Cancore plans to launch its CNRX token, but Rashid did not give an estimated timeline. He said users who stake the token will get lower trading fees and higher limits for trading and AI tools. Liquidity providers will also receive token benefits. Rashid previously co-founded blockchain security firm BlockApex, which he said completed more than 125 audits and helped secure over $3.2 billion in assets. Cancore was founded in late 2025 and has 10 employees, mainly based in the UAE and Pakistan, Rashid said. It plans to hire more people for engineering, security, AI infrastructure and institutional business development. title: Brazilian companies turned to stablecoins on election day to dodge a currency crash
text:
Brazilian companies entered a crypto trading frenzy on Sunday to protect their treasuries from the outcome of an election that saw incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, known as Lula, unexpectedly beat Flávio Bolsonaro.
Corporate accounts generated 78% of trading on crypto exchange Mercado Bitcoin, with turnover in Tether’s dollar-pegged stablecoin, USDT, jumping nearly 800% from the week before and more than triple the average of the four preceding Sundays. Trading in bitcoin BTC$84,459.46 surged 865% compared with the previous Sunday, the exchange said.
Lula’s platform of increased social spending and a ban on online betting that would reduce tax income sparked concerns the country’s finances would suffer if he won, adding to pressure on the real and keeping borrowing costs high. Rising debt, new spending commitments and limited scope for tax increases would make that task harder.
“For investors, this reinforces the logic of not relying only on the real,” Pedro Fontes, a research analyst at Mercado Bitcoin, wrote in an analysis shared with CoinDesk. “In this scenario of higher exchange rate pressure, stablecoins, such as USDT and USDC, are a simple way to dollarize part of your assets, at any time and starting from low amounts.”
Stronger opposition in Congress could complicate efforts to address fiscal problems, reinforcing the appeal of assets whose prices are set in global markets, he said.
Corporate concerns materialized the next day, when the benchmark Ibovespa stock index crashed 14% in its worst performance since March 2020 and the dollar jumped more than 8% against the real, its largest daily gain since 1999.
The response had been different three weeks earlier, when Bolsonaro finished ahead of Lula in the first round of voting. The Ibovespa jumped 7.7% and the dollar weakened more than 4% against the real as investors anticipated a change of government and tighter control over public spending.
Lula´s victory made him the first presidential candidate in Brazil’s modern democracy to secure a victory after finishing in second place. Even so, Brazil’s companies took a cautious stance.
“The main driver of volume was companies seeking to protect their treasuries,” Mercado Bitcoin said. “Retail customers were responsible for just 22% of trading volume, while MB’s corporate clients generated 78% of the total for Sunday.”
Corporate clients are known to hold up to 15% of their assets on the platform.
The burst of real-denominated trading extended beyond Mercado Bitcoin. Data from Biscoint, which tracks crypto prices and volume across 10 venues including Binance and MB, shows turnover in USDT, the largest stablecoin, against the real rose 150% from the previous Sunday. Volume in USDC, the second-largest, jumped 318%.
The surge extended into Monday, with combined USDT and USDC turnover reaching 1.84 billion reais ($350 million), 65% higher than in the previous week, while bitcoin trading rose more than ninefold to 1,336 BTC.
The increases came as volumes fell elsewhere. On Binance, for example, bitcoin turnover against the real rose 370% while the global BTC/USDT pair recorded a 25% decline.
Bitcoin gained 9.4% against the real while slipping 0.2% against USDT, consistent with a repricing of Brazil’s currency as investors reacted to the election.
The expectation of a Bolsonaro victory was also reflected in prediction markets. In an Oct. 24 preview, Kalshi put his chances of winning at 84%, even as its own article described polling as showing an exceedingly close race.
Kalshi and Polymarket have both been blocked in Brazil since April.
Lula won the runoff the next day, in an election that included a controversial last-minute two-hour extension to voting time granted by Lula’s former defense attorney.
“[Prediction markets] were trading the first-round result, poll headlines and the story built around them,” Einar Knobel, CEO and co-founder of sports data and technology company TxODDS, told CoinDesk in an emailed statement.
“I would not read this as a failure of prediction markets,” Knobel said. “The mechanism did what it is designed to do with the information it was given.”

title: Crypto.com and OG.com launch US crypto perps with up to 5x leverage
text: Crypto exchange Crypto.com and its derivatives partner OG.com began rolling out crypto perpetual futures to "eligible" U.S. traders on Tuesday. The contracts offer up to 5x leverage and let traders bet on rising or falling crypto prices with no expiration date. The offering comes with typical take-profit and stop-loss orders and isolated margin. The Tuesday release did not specify eligibility requirements. Crypto.com said it recently registered as an introducing broker with the National Futures Association to be able to offer the perps. The products run through OG.com's "CFTC-regulated exchange and clearinghouse and futures commission merchant." The launch follows the CFTC's May decision to open the U.S. markets to crypto perpetuals. The agency approved Kalshi's bitcoin perps and issued a no-action relief for Coinbase to offer digital commodity derivatives. Kraken then launched U.S. perps on Kraken Pro in June, following its acquisition of Bitnomial. Crypto.com is also looking to push into stock derivatives. Nadex, the exchange operating under OG.com, registered with the SEC to trade security futures last month. At the time, CEO Kris Marszalek said the company was also working with the SEC and CFTC to offer single-stock perpetual futures. Ondo Perps CEO David Wells told The Block in September that U.S. perpetuals are a "huge opportunity," though offshore platforms would need different clearing and settlement arrangements to meet U.S. rules.

title: Circle Pushes Deeper Into Latin America With USDC Settlement in Colombia - Decrypt
text:
Circle is extending its reach across Latin America, teaming up with payments-technology firm ACI Worldwide to fold USDC settlement into the region’s existing banking rails, starting with a pilot in Colombia.
Announced Tuesday, the collaboration pairs Circle’s USDC infrastructure with ACI Connetic, ACI’s cloud-based payments orchestration platform, to show financial institutions how stablecoin settlement can run alongside traditional payment systems rather than replace them.
The initial focus is Colombia, where ACI built the central infrastructure behind Bre-B, the country’s interoperable instant-payments network. The idea is to test how a digital dollar like USDC can slot into that real-time, account-to-account system to create what the companies call a multi-rail ecosystem.
The framing reflects a shift in how banks are approaching stablecoins. Rather than debating the technology itself, institutions increasingly want to know how digital dollars fit into the treasury operations, governance and settlement processes they already run.
“The conversation around stablecoins is moving from possibility to practicality,” said Craig Ramsey, ACI’s global head of account-to-account payments, describing the effort as a way to integrate regulated stablecoins into workflows banks already trust.
Kash Razzaghi, Circle’s chief commercial officer, said financial institutions across Latin America are increasingly looking at how stablecoins can support the evolution of payments “within the infrastructure they already use,” framing USDC as a bridge between traditional finance and the digital economy.
The move builds on Circle’s steady regional expansion. The company has pushed into dozens of emerging markets as stablecoins go mainstream, and earlier gained a Latin American foothold when Argentina’s Mercado Pago added USDC.
Colombia is a logical next target, given high cross-border remittance volumes and a population well-acquainted with dollar-denominated savings as a hedge against inflation.
Circle positioned the pilot as technology-agnostic: while it runs on USDC, ACI’s platform is built to support other payment networks and digital-asset providers over time. For Circle, the deal is another step in weaving its stablecoin into the plumbing of mainstream finance, this time in a fast-growing payments market where instant-payment adoption is already accelerating.

title: Ripple's RLUSD stablecoin is coming to Robinhood's app, potentially reaching millions
text:
Ripple’s RLUSD stablecoin is set to reach Robinhood’s retail customers later this year, giving the dollar-backed token access to a brokerage platform with roughly 28.6 million funded accounts.
“From bringing RLUSD to retail and institutional markets to helping Robinhood manage its own treasury operations, this partnership reflects growing institutional demand for integrated solutions that support customer-facing offerings and core financial operations,” said Monica Long, president of Ripple.
The companies announced the partnership on Tuesday. RLUSD is already available on Robinhood Chain and Bitstamp, the crypto exchange Robinhood acquired for $200 million in June. Now, RLUSD is also expected to become available through the Robinhood app before the end of 2026.
That decision puts Robinhood in an unusual position, as it helped establish the Global Dollar Network in 2024 to promote USDG, a competing stablecoin issued by Paxos. Now, Robinhood is announcing its plans to offer Ripple’s rival token to its customers.
The Global Dollar Network, founded in 2024, brings together companies that help distribute USDG and share in the revenue it generates. The arrangement gives members a financial incentive to promote USDG, but Robinhood’s partnership with Ripple shows that those incentives do not preclude members from offering competing stablecoins. Other founding members included Kraken, Galaxy Digital, Anchorage Digital and CoinDesk's parent company, Bullish. Arbitrum joined earlier this month.
Robinhood has already given USDG a role in its products. In July, the consortium announced that USDG would be the default lending asset for Robinhood Earn, its onchain lending product.
Robinhood did not announce any changes to its USDG agreement, and it remains unclear whether RLUSD will be offered alongside USDG in the same products. CoinDesk contacted Robinhood regarding this matter, but the fintech did not respond immediately.
Robinhood reported 28.6 million funded customers at the end of August. The companies have not said how many will be eligible to use RLUSD when it becomes available in the app.
The partnership also covers Robinhood’s institutional business. Bitstamp will use RLUSD on the XRP Ledger for settlement, while Robinhood plans to adopt Ripple’s treasury software for cash management, payments and forecasting.
Ripple Prime already provides Bitstamp with lending and margin financing across roughly 20 digital assets. The companies plan to add perpetual futures trading later this year.
RLUSD, launched in December 2024, has grown to a market capitalization of more than $2.5 billion, according to the press release.
Robinhood has not said whether RLUSD will receive the same role as USDG in its lending products, or how the two stablecoins will be promoted to customers.
Also on Tuesday, Ripple, which got final Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) approval to go ahead with the Ripple National Trust Bank (RNTB) yesterday, announced the expansion of its partnership with BNY (BNY) to broaden institutional digital asset custody infrastructure and explore new institutional use cases for blockchain, including tokenized trade. Both firms first partnered in July 2025.

title: Next Week’s Midterms Will Change U.S. Crypto Policy: Analyst
text:
TD Cowen says a Democratic sweep would stall the CLARITY Act, while regulators keep advancing rules that favor the crypto sector.
Washington’s crypto agenda hinges on next week’s midterm elections, according to a new policy note from TD Cowen, shared with Bitcoin Magazine.
Analyst Jaret Seiberg warned in the note that the probable results could make it difficult for Congress to pass the CLARITY Act over the next two years. The bill would set the rules for bitcoin and other digital assets, and the industry has spent $176 million on more than 100 races to shape the outcome. Here are a couple of the results:
Prediction markets cited in the report give Democrats a 90% chance of winning the House and a 62% chance of winning the Senate. TD Cowen considers this the most negative scenario for bitcoin and the broader crypto sector. Under it, Sen. Elizabeth Warren would become Senate Banking Committee chair. Seiberg describes her as a crypto skeptic who has led opposition to the CLARITY Act, and he expects her to conduct tough oversight of federal regulators.
Warren cannot stop regulators from adopting policies that favor the industry. Seiberg expects President Trump to remain favorable toward crypto, so he would veto any bill that limits his regulators’ authority. Democrats would lack the votes to override him. As a result, policy changes are expected to focus on tokenization, perpetual futures, and stablecoins.
The second scenario keeps Democrats in control of the House while key Senate races stay close enough to break for Republicans. Sen. Tim Scott would keep his Banking Committee gavel. TD Cowen views this outcome as a better result for bitcoin, because Rep. Maxine Waters could trade support for parts of the market structure bill in exchange for investor protections and action on her other priorities.
Adverse legislation would be blocked from reaching the president’s desk.
Kalshi gives Republicans a 10% chance to keep the House and a 35% chance to keep the Senate. TD Cowen calls this the best path for crypto policy, though the margins matter. A wider Senate majority would improve the odds that leaders advance the CLARITY Act in 2027 or 2028, and they could attempt a revival during the lame-duck session.
A narrow majority, by contrast, would leave the bill stalled, as Democrats keep pushing ethics provisions that the president opposes. When the Senate blocked the bill, Bitcoin-related stocks tumbled.
For background, the CLARITY Act would create federal rules for digital assets. The House passed its version in July 2025 by a 294-134 vote. The Senate Banking Committee approved its own version in May 2026 by a 15-9 vote, with two Democrats joining Republicans.
On the Senate floor, a cloture vote failed 49-50 on September 15. Democrats want ethics language that would bar senior officials, including the president, from profiting from crypto ventures. Republicans and industry groups resist those limits. Stablecoin yield is another dispute. Each side says the other is blocking progress, and the bill is stuck.

title: Ipsos Poll Finds More Americans Support FinTech Not Tied To Crypto
text:
The September survey offered a possible window into US voters who could consider fintech and digital asset policies on Election Day.
A new poll from the DeFi Education Fund and Ipsos found that 72% of people surveyed said it was “somewhat” to “extremely” important for politicians to be supportive of policies encouraging financial technology built in the US.
On Tuesday, Ipsos released the results of a poll of 1,545 people conducted in September, showing that 35% of respondents said it was “very” or “extremely” important for political candidates to support the idea of “ensuring that those who are building the next generation of financial technology are encouraged to do so in the United States.” An additional 37% of those surveyed said that the fintech policy was “somewhat important.”
Notably, only 9% of the Ipsos poll respondents said that they were familiar with crypto, and 5% with stablecoins. A majority, 87%, said that they had not held any digital assets in the previous 12 months. Only 13% said it was “very” or “extremely” important for a political candidate to encourage growth in blockchain, crypto, and DeFi.
“Ownership of crypto and openness to DeFi are largely consistent with 2025, and interest looks consistent across party lines,” said Ipsos.
The poll was conducted about two months before Americans were set to vote on the next session of Congress in the 2026 midterm elections, in which crypto policies and laws could be a factor at the polling stations. Political action committees backed by crypto companies have already spent tens of millions of dollars in an attempt to influence voters in key races.

title: Intel, Oracle, IBM join growing list of firms objecting to OKX–ICE tokenized stock plans
text:
IBM, Oracle, Intel and IonQ have opted out of plans by crypto exchange OKX and NYSE parent Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) to offer blockchain-based trading of their shares, bringing the total number of issuer objections to 26.
The four companies were named in an updated public notice dated Monday, Oct. 26, from OKXICE, the two firms’ joint venture. They join earlier objectors including Microsoft, Alphabet, Goldman Sachs, Cisco and Wells Fargo.
The growing list underscores a hurdle for OKXICE and the SEC’s new framework for tokenized stock trading: building a market that issuers are willing to join. The agency’s five-year “Innovation Exemption” gives qualifying venues room to test round-the-clock blockchain-based trading of stocks, and it also gives public companies an option to block their shares from being offered.
OKXICE issued its initial public notice on Oct. 4, outlining plans to use Uniswap v4 liquidity pools on OKX’s XLayer blockchain, with transactions settled in stablecoins. The venue would use automated market makers — software that executes trades through pools of assets rather than matching buyers and sellers through a conventional order book.
Under the framework, venues must notify issuers and give them 30 days to object before offering tokenized versions of their shares.
All four newly disclosed objectors were among the 62 companies in OKXICE’s original proposed roster. That brings objections from the original selection to 23, or about 37%, according to a CoinDesk tally. The overall count also includes Cerebras Systems, Arm Holdings and Wells Fargo, which were absent from that from the original selection.
The growing list of objections highlights early issuer caution about plans to trade their shares under the SEC’s new framework. The rules give companies a say in how their shares come onchain, but also tilts the decision toward opting out, industry experts told CoinDesk’s Tokenization Weekly. Objecting costs nothing, while staying silent allows trading to begin without a mechanism to withdraw that consent later. For legal and investor-relations teams still getting familiar with the arrangements, saying no leaves more time to understand them.
The financial benefit for issuers is also uncertain yet. Tokenization could bring additional demand, particularly from overseas investors, but that may not be enough to offset concerns about thin, round-the-clock trading outside the familiar market structure, TD Securities’ Reid Noch previously told CoinDesk.
Andrew Cuomo, OKXICE’s co-chairman and former New York governor, previously described the objections as expected, with many companies rather “wait and see how it goes rather than be the first to participate,” he said during a press call last week.

title: Bitcoin Wallet Maker Keystone Pulls Devices as Stolen Key Opens Door to Fakes - Decrypt
text:
Keystone, a maker of Bitcoin hardware wallets that keep the secret codes controlling your crypto offline, said Monday it will destroy 18,835 unsold devices after attackers obtained the key that proves its hardware is genuine. The company has also suspended shipping of all unshipped orders from its website.
For buyers, the risk is a counterfeit wallet that looks brand new and passes Keystone’s own verification check, because the attacker obtained the key that the check relies on. A criminal could then sell such a device to someone who loads real savings onto it.
“If it is exposed, an attacker could use it to produce counterfeit devices that pass authentication checks,” Keystone said in its statement. “These devices could then be sold or shipped to customers, who might unknowingly use them as genuine products, potentially resulting in asset theft.”
Keystone calls it a WebAuth key, a secret code written into each device at the factory so a page on the company’s website can confirm the hardware is real. It cannot be erased or rewritten, and the 18,835 units in inventory that carry it are being destroyed rather than sold.
Keystone first said Saturday that a third party had obtained customer shipping information. Monday’s statement added the stolen key and a count of 25,964 affected buyer records, but it does not say who is responsible or when the attacker first got in.
The incident affected records from Keystone’s Shopify store, the e-commerce platform that handled its online sales. Keystone says 51,083 buyer records were involved, but 25,119 had already had their personal information erased, leaving 25,964 from 2024 to 2026 that still held names, contact details, shipping addresses and order information. Purchases through Amazon and other channels were not affected.
Some of that data should already have been deleted. Keystone’s policy was to erase buyer records after 180 days, and the automated bulk-deletion tool it built for the job did not work reliably.
“Some erasure tasks failed, and we did not detect and address these failures in time, resulting in certain personal information being retained beyond the permitted period,” Keystone said. “We failed to fulfill our commitment to erase customer data on time, and we accept responsibility for this failure.”
Customer lists are a recurring weak point for wallet makers. Ledger’s 2020 leak eventually reached about 292,000 customers, and those who received phishing emails afterward worried they could become targets of home invasions.

Trezor and SafePal each disclosed customer-data breaches in August, affecting 13,689 customers and about 39,798 customers, respectively.
Names and addresses matter because of wrench attacks, in which criminals use threats or violence to force owners to hand over their crypto. Chainalysis counted 46 violent attacks in the first half of 2026, with more than $30 million stolen.
The manufacturer also warned of scammers offering “asset migration,” “wallet verification” or “investigation assistance.”
“We will not ask you to return your device,” the company said. “Anyone contacting you under the pretext of a ‘recall’ and asking you to ship your device to them should be treated as a scammer.”
Sales on Keystone’s website will switch to preorders until production of devices with a new key is complete, and the company says it has submitted reports to authorities in the EU, UK, and other jurisdictions.
Keystone cut its retention period for customer data from 180 days to 90 and asked Shopify on October 24 to erase all overdue buyer data, a process with a 10-day waiting period. The company expects the erasure to finish on November 3.
